To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most suitable battery technology depends on the specific energy storage application.

Lithium ion batteries are the best choice for energy storage applications where fast response and high power is required (e.g. frequency regulation), while Vanadium redox batteries are the most appropriate for applications where long life time and high energy density is required (e. g. load shifting).
Lithium ion batteries are suitable for short-term energy storage, with the highest efficiency of the three technologies, and are the most expensive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis and modeling of different battery technologies for the large-scale energy storage applications.
the development of the battery technologies for large-scale energy storage applications.
the development of a methodology that will enable the selection of the best technology for energy storage in the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all of the three technologies can be successfully used in the energy storage applications.
the Lithium ion battery technology is the most mature and suitable for large scale energy storages, but it is not the best solution for all applications.
all of these battery technologies are very promising and have the ability to fulfill the requirements of large scale energy storage systems.
